applicable_programme.grade_mapping_note: The public MYP page describes the programme as for students aged 11-16 and as a five-year programme that schools may shorten. Mapping Grade 7 (often about ages 12-13) onto that span is our convention, not an IB grade or MYP-year boundary.

grade_specific_note.label: C
grade_specific_note.text: Florida Grade 7 social studies is grade-based civics, economics, geography, and one history-of-communism benchmark (SS.7), not an MYP integrated-humanities eAssessment syllabus. The shared Grades 6-8 band (SS.68.AA and SS.68.HE, 15 benchmarks) is stored in the grade-7 Florida file as the single copy and is included in this alignment so it is not dropped. Those codes are not grade-7-only. Grade 8 must not copy them again. They are not IB learning outcomes.

subject_group_or_structure.mapping_to_primer_subject: Grade 7 Florida social studies (SS.7 civics, economics, geography, and history of communism, plus the shared SS.68 band housed in this grade’s Florida file) is mapped here to MYP individuals and societies. The public page allows discrete courses such as history, geography, economics, and civics, or an integrated humanities course. It does not require this Florida list.

official_requirements.label: B
official_requirements.text: The International Baccalaureate® (IB) Middle Years Programme (MYP) is for students aged 11-16.

official_requirements.label: B
official_requirements.text: The MYP is a five-year programme, which can be implemented in a partnership between schools, or in several abbreviated (two, three or four year) formats.

official_requirements.label: B
official_requirements.text: Developing and applying these social, thinking, research, communication and self management skills helps students learn how to learn.

official_requirements.label: B
official_requirements.text: Using global contexts, MYP students develop an understanding of their common humanity and shared guardianship of the planet through developmentally appropriate explorations of: identities and relationships; personal and cultural expression; orientations in space and time; scientific and technical innovation; fairness and development; globalization and sustainability.

official_requirements.label: B
official_requirements.text: The MYP prescribes sixteen key interdisciplinary concepts along with related concepts for each discipline.

official_requirements.label: B
official_requirements.text: MYP teachers assess the prescribed subject-group objectives using the assessment criteria for each subject group in each year of the programme.

official_requirements.label: B
official_requirements.text: Individuals and societies incorporates disciplines traditionally studied in the humanities, as well as disciplines in the social sciences.

official_requirements.label: B
official_requirements.text: In this subject group, students collect, describe and analyse data used in studies of societies, test hypotheses, and learn how to interpret complex information, including original source material.

official_requirements.label: B
official_requirements.text: Schools can organize the study of individuals and societies in the MYP as discrete courses, modular courses, or integrated courses. Discrete-course examples named on the page include history, geography, economics, and civics.

official_requirements.label: B
official_requirements.text: The individuals and societies subject brief names four equally weighted assessment criteria: A Knowing and understanding; B Investigating; C Communicating; D Thinking critically. The 1-8 band descriptors are not stored here.

typical_fit.label: C
typical_fit.text: Grade 7 Florida social studies in this draft is a civics sequence (founding ideas, the Constitution, citizenship, the three branches, and foreign policy) plus economics, geography of the United States and North America, and one history-of-communism benchmark. The same Florida file also holds the shared Grades 6-8 African American History and Holocaust Education benchmarks (SS.68). MYP individuals and societies asks students to investigate societies and to use sources. It does not set the Florida document list, the SS.68 content, or a Grade 7 placement. Grade 6 omitted SS.68. This grade is their single home. Grade 8 should not align them again.

suggested_alignment_to_florida_and_arizo.label: C

florida.alignment_note: Analyzing ideas and grievances in the Declaration of Independence can be studied in a civics or history course under criterion A. That document and its grievances are Florida content, not an IB objective.

Separation of powers, checks and balances, individual rights, rule of law, and due process are Florida constitutional benchmarks. The public MYP page names civics as a possible discrete course, not this list.
Applying rights in the Bill of Rights and other amendments is a Florida civics benchmark. The public MYP pages do not name those amendments.
Supply, demand, choice, scarcity, and opportunity cost fit economics, which the page names as a possible discipline. Those terms in this sentence are Florida’s.
Locating the fifty states, their capitals, and the nation’s capital fits geography as a possible course. That map list is Florida’s.

Assessing effects of communist governments on freedom, political participation, and the economy is a Florida History of Communism benchmark. The public MYP pages retrieved do not name communism. This row does not turn that sentence into an IB outcome.

Identifying Afro-Eurasian trade routes before the Atlantic slave trade is Florida content in the shared Grades 6-8 band, stored only in the grade-7 file. MYP may include a history course. It does not require this benchmark.

The Holocaust benchmark is Florida’s SS.68.HE.1.1, housed once in Grade 7 for the Grades 6-8 band. A history inquiry can study it under criterion B. The benchmark sentence is not an IB learning outcome, and Grade 8 must not duplicate the code.

suggested_alignment_to_florida_and_arizo.notes: Arizona standards deferred. These rows are suggested starting points (Label C), not an official IB-Florida crosswalk.
